name: Competitor battlecard
summary: Your salespeople get one page on one named competitor: where it is strong, where you are stronger and the proof, what to say when it comes up, and the questions to ask. Nothing about the competitor goes on the card without a dated source; anything unsupported is held back for the approver.

sources.title: Its own rules for a card salespeople can stand behind: every line tagged to a dated source, a recheck date set by the oldest source used, stale pages and unsupported lines held back for the approver, silence reported as no mention found, buyer reports kept apart from facts, and a head-to-head count from the deal export that shows no rate on too few deals.

sources.contribution: The honest shape of the card: the competitor's real strengths, our advantages each with proof and a question that brings it out, early questions that steer a conversation to our advantages, objection answers with a follow-up question, topics not to raise first, the deals better left to the competitor, nothing said about the competitor that cannot be checked, sources on the card and a ninety-day refresh.

Each point set out as what is true, why it matters to the deal and what to say (a structure the package credits to a published battlecard framework); a short answer with one follow-up question for when the competitor is mentioned in passing; a price comparison showing what each side includes and costs extra; acknowledging the competitor's strength before the difference; and keeping prices current.
